prompt: Review cloud security for an AWS organization with prod and non-prod accounts. Engineers currently have IAM users with long-lived keys, an EKS workload uses the node role, a cross-account analytics role trusts the whole source account, one S3 bucket policy grants broad read to that role, KMS grants are undocumented, and CloudTrail is account-local. Redesign human federation and emergency access, workload-specific temporary identity, cross-account trust conditions and resource scope, S3/KMS permissions, organization guardrails, public-access posture, and centralized protected audit logs. Show how to verify the effective allow/deny paths with actual IAM/resource-policy analysis and safe test calls. Pod/container privilege itself belongs to infrastructure-security.

requirements: EKS workload and node-role identity paths

falsifiableChecks.assertion: Standing human IAM access keys are replaced by federated/temporary access where feasible, root/emergency access is separately protected, and privileged paths are explicitly audited.
The EKS workload uses a workload-specific role/identity rather than inheriting the broader node role, with only the service actions/resources it needs.
Cross-account role trust and S3/KMS resource permissions are constrained to the intended principal/actions/resources/conditions rather than trusting an entire account plus broad bucket/key access.
Organization/account guardrails and public-access policy are explicit, preventive where appropriate, and tested against a representative prohibited configuration.
Cloud control-plane and relevant resource-policy changes are centrally logged to a protected destination with evidence that workload/account admins cannot silently erase the primary audit trail.
The review verifies both intended allowed calls and representative cross-account/public/escalation denials using provider policy analysis and/or safe non-production calls.
